title: EncounterEvent
description: One creature's testimony about meeting another individuated creature — peer-to-peer, not reader-to-text and not engine-inference-over-text. Same firewall reasoning as ReactionEvent@1, one register over: an EncounterEvent is an OBSERVATION BY ONE REFERENT OF ANOTHER, never an engine inference, so it lives in its own append-only log rather than the semantic ledger — it carries no operator, no prior_id, and no operator_epoch, and it may never mint an observation, referent, hypothesis, or task about the peer it describes. self_id and peer_id must differ and are referent ids, not name strings (docs/nameless-referent.md: same-string identity is never assumed). kind is a closed, DECLARED vocabulary — never inferred from payload content (cube/index.js's dead-ends: a coordinate that gates is derived from a declaration). ts and seq are HOST-SUPPLIED and never generated engine-side, for the same replay-determinism reason as ReactionEvent@1.

encounter_id.description: Content address of every other field. encounter:sha256:<64 hex>.

self_id.description: The individuated creature testifying. A referent id, not a name string.

peer_id.description: The individuated creature encountered. Must differ from self_id — a creature does not encounter itself.

world_id.description: The shared substrate the encounter happened within (a machine, a room, a corpus context) — the stigmergic commons both creatures wrote to, not a merged state.

ts.description: Host-supplied milliseconds since the Unix epoch. The engine never reads an ambient clock.

seq.description: Host-supplied per-(self,world) monotone counter. Gives the log a total order independent of clock resolution.

kind.description: The four declared encounter kinds. withdraw is disengagement, not a negative valence — nothing in this spec assigns kinds a sign, because weighting them against each other is an inference deferred until the channel has data (same discipline as ReactionEvent@1's skip/abandon).

context.description: What medium the encounter happened over — creatures on one machine may be specialized to different perceiver modalities (text, audio, video), so this is required to read an encounter against what each party could actually perceive.

payload.description: Kind-specific detail. May carry a DECLARED valence/arousal or a proposed prior update (for kind=teach), but the engine never computes these from content — they are asserted by the emitting creature or absent. Deliberately unconstrained: the channel collects first and the shapes are not yet known.
